verdict.rationale: Buzz's self-hosting docs describe a distinct 'Quickstart (eval)' Helm profile (in-cluster Postgres/Redis/MinIO, auto-generated secrets) separate from the 'Production' profile with external managed data stores, and a single-node/VPS compose bundle with 'no external services required' — implying an AI-native user could stand up an isolated instance for testing rather than touching a production deployment. There's also an agent-behavior benchmark suite (buzz-dataset) that exercises agent actions in a controlled test harness. However, there is no explicit sandbox/staging mode within a single running instance, no documented data-seeding or reset tooling, and no first-party statement guaranteeing test isolation from production data. Missing for 10: an explicit sandbox/staging environment feature (not just a separate self-hosted deployment), documented test-data seeding/reset tooling, and independent confirmation that eval deployments safely avoid production data.
